printers.plugin_updates_hint: {count} plugin updates: open the store to apply
printers.remove_summary: This deletes the printer from Bespok3d on this computer. Your printer keeps running.
printers.remove_detail: Bespok3d forgets this printer: its record, pinned certificate, and saved settings are removed from this app. Nothing on the printer changes unless you also choose to remove Bespok3d from it below. You can add the printer again later.
printers.remove_also_teardown: Also remove Bespok3d from the printer
printers.remove_also_teardown_hint: Uninstalls all plugins and the daemon on the device first. This cannot be undone.
printers.force_hint: Re-run a setup flow on demand
printers.custom_ssh: My SSH credentials are not the default ones
printers.custom_ssh_hint: When on, Bespok3d asks for your SSH user and password before each operation. When off, it uses the printer's factory login.
printers.deactivated_hint: Bespok3d is deactivated on this printer.
printers.deactivate_summary: Bespok3d will be hidden. Your printer works normally. You can reactivate anytime.
printers.deactivate_detail: Plugin services will be stopped. Autostart entries, printer.cfg and moonraker.conf include lines, and the init hook in S90lmd will be removed. All plugin files are kept intact. After reboot the printer runs stock: no plugins, no daemon. Reactivate from the main window or Settings → Printers to bring everything back.
printers.uninstall_summary: This permanently removes Bespok3d and all plugins. It cannot be undone.
printers.uninstall_detail: All plugins will be uninstalled and their patches reverted. The daemon, workspace directory (/userdata/bespok3d), and all configuration changes (printer.cfg, moonraker.conf, nginx, S90lmd) will be removed. Only Bespok3d's own links are taken back from printer_data/config/bespok3d; any files you put there yourself are kept. The printer record will be deleted from this app. To use Bespok3d again you will need to re-enroll.

safety_recovery.guidance: This usually means the plugin has a bug or needs an update for your firmware. You do not need to fix anything yourself: report it to the plugin's author, or check whether a newer version is available. Your printer keeps working in the meantime.

install_error.guidance: This usually means a problem with the plugin itself, not your printer. You can try again, or report it to the plugin's author so they can fix it. Nothing on your printer was changed.
uninstall_error.title: Could not remove {name}
uninstall_error.subtitle: The plugin could not be removed. Your printer was not changed.
uninstall_error.guidance: Your printer is unchanged: the plugin is still installed and working. You can try removing it again, or report the problem so it can be fixed.
install_refused.title: {name} was not installed
install_refused.subtitle: This package failed a security check. Your printer was not changed.
install_malformed.title: {name} is packaged incorrectly
install_malformed.subtitle: The plugin's package is built wrong, so your printer safely refused it. Your printer was not changed.
install_malformed.guidance: This copy of the plugin includes files that are not part of its signed contents, so it cannot be trusted and was not installed. That is a defect in how the plugin was packaged, not a problem with your printer, and reinstalling will not fix it. It needs a corrected release from the plugin's author. The files listed below are the ones that do not belong; sharing them helps the author fix it.

install_malformed.reason.escaping_member: These files would be written outside the plugin's own folder:
install_malformed.reason.checksum_mismat: These files do not match the package's signed manifest:
install_malformed.reason.escaping_plugin: The package's plugin name is not valid.
install_malformed.reason.unknown: The package failed an integrity check:

add.custom_ssh_hint: Leave this off if you haven't changed your printer's factory login. Turn it on to enter your own SSH user and password during enrollment.
enroll.propose_summary: Bespok3d can enroll this printer: it installs a small on-printer service so you can manage plugins from here.
enroll.propose_detail: Enrollment connects over SSH, deploys the Bespok3d daemon, and prepares the printer. It takes a couple of minutes and the printer may restart its services. You can do this later instead from the printer menu.
enroll.ssh_closed_summary: {name} is not accepting SSH connections, so Bespok3d cannot set it up yet.
enroll.ssh_closed_detail: Enrollment runs over SSH (port 22), which is closed. On the printer's screen, turn on root access (developer mode / SSH) in the printer settings, then press Retry. If you just enabled it, give the printer a few seconds to start the SSH service.
gen.show_installed_hint: When you open a printer, skip the catalog and jump straight to what's installed.
gen.telemetry_hint: It tells us which parts of Bespok3d get used and which ones break. Change your mind whenever you like; it takes effect straight away.
gen.telemetry_sent_actions: That the app started, and a handful of things done with it: a printer enrolled, a plugin installed, the app updated.
gen.telemetry_sent_result: When something breaks, the kind of break and which part of the app it happened in. Your app version goes with all of it.
gen.telemetry_sent_client: The kind of app (desktop), the operating system it runs on, and the language it is set to.
gen.telemetry_never_typed: Anything you type: no names, no addresses, no passwords, no keys.
gen.telemetry_never_printer: Anything about your printers: no serial numbers, no network addresses, no file names.
gen.telemetry_never_location: Anything about where you are: no country, no town, nothing. The internet address your connection arrives on is never looked up, and is never kept with what you send.
gen.telemetry_never_text: Error messages and stack traces. Only the kind of error is sent, never its text.
gen.telemetry_never_id: Anything that tells your copy of Bespok3d apart from anyone else's. There is no installation id, and nothing that names you is ever sent: every copy reports as simply Bespok3d.
gen.telemetry_off_note: Turning this off stops anything further being sent. It cannot take back what was already sent.
gen.telemetry_ask_summary: Bespok3d is built by a very small team, and knowing which parts get used and which ones break is how we decide what to work on. It is your call, and you can change it later in Settings, General.
gen.plugin_defaults_hint: Shared values every printer inherits: pre-fill install fields, changeable before installing. Fields set per printer live in the Per printer view.
gen.defaults_per_printer_hint: Values set here apply to the selected printer only and replace the shared value. Clearing one falls back to the shared value.
gen.defaults_selected_printer_hint: Following the printer selected in the header. Switch printers there.

gen.defaults_none_installed: No installed plugin has editable settings. Switch to All plugins to browse every default.
gen.defaults_none_per_printer: No per-printer fields yet. A field moves here when its plugin sets it per printer, or when you flip one to This printer here or in the plugin's Config tab.

keys.purpose.default_tip: Default key, used for all unassigned cases
keys.row.delete_warn_brief: Deleting this key is permanent. Your published identity will be removed and anything you signed will become unverified. Printers enrolled with this key will lose your access.
keys.row.delete_warn_detail: The private key is erased from this device with no recovery. If the key was published, its file is automatically removed from your bespok3d-publisher repo; anyone looking up packages signed by this fingerprint will find nothing, and the trust tier drops to unknown (yellow). Printers that enrolled this key for mutual authentication will reject your connections; removing the key from each printer's access list requires SSH. Signed packages and lists still install for others, but without identity.

adapters.intro: Adapters connect bespok3d to specific printer models. Each adapter defines SSH connection defaults, the steps needed to install bespok3d, and how to verify a successful enrollment.
adapters.jinni_desc: Jinni (daemon-side half): its version and any interface extensions are reported by a connected, managed printer.
create.lib.title: Your macro library
create.lib.sub: Every macro you save lives here and can be dropped onto any printer. Saving is the gentle on-ramp to sharing: a saved macro is already a real, portable plugin.
create.lib.starters_note: curated, one line of plain description each
create.pub.title: Publish to the world
create.pub.sub: Sign a build with your key and push it where anyone can install it. This is designed and ready in the UI; it switches on when signing ships.
create.pub.gate_body: The whole flow below is built. It stays inactive until the signing work lands, so nothing here can be pressed yet. Until then, the loop that matters already works: build and test on your own printer.
create.pub.step1_sub: The freshest .b3 from the workbench. Version and checksums come from the build, you do not manage them.
create.pub.step2_sub: With a GPG key from Settings. Anyone, not just Bespok3d users, can verify a signed package against your published public key.
create.pub.step3_sub: A package gets a stable identity and a deep link. Pushing a curated list (a registry) uses the very same model.
create.pub.cta_note_pre: Opens when signing ships. Manage signing keys in
create.pub.cta_note_post: so you are ready the moment it does.
create.macro.title: Add a macro
create.macro.sub: Give it a name, adjust a couple of lines, and send it to a printer. No manifest, no jargon. It installs as a real plugin you can remove later.
create.macro.step1_title: Pick a starter, or write your own
create.macro.step3_hint: turn on Explain if any line looks unfamiliar
create.macro.summary_rest: Nothing else changes. It becomes a removable plugin, and a copy is saved to your Library so you can reuse it on other printers.
create.macro.reveal1_title: See the generated Klipper config and tunable settings
create.macro.written_to_printer: What gets written to the printer
create.macro.tunable_settings: Tunable settings · the form your installer fills in
create.macro.reveal2_title: See the full manifest, or open this in the workbench
create.macro.real_plugin_pre: This macro is a real plugin already.
create.macro.real_plugin_post: to add files, services, or store metadata, then build and publish.
create.sec.files_blurb: Sort each file into what it is, not where it goes. Bespok3d turns a class into a real path on the printer, so a package can never write somewhere it should not.
create.sec.imported_meta: 18 files - 412 KB - imported from a folder
create.sec.classes_grow: The list of classes grows as new kinds of plugin are packaged. Nothing here is a fixed menu.
create.sec.variables_blurb: These become the form your installer fills in. You are designing the consumer's experience right here. Portable settings only, never real paths.
create.sec.services_blurb: Declare what this plugin offers and what it leans on. Bespok3d resolves the rest against whatever is installed, so you never hardcode another plugin.
create.sec.capability_desc: a capability other plugins can require
create.sec.managed_blurb: For a plugin that runs a process. You declare the command and Bespok3d generates the init script. No scripts ship inside the package.
create.sec.command_hint: Variables in braces are filled from the installer's answers.
create.sec.start_auto_hint: Launch on boot and keep it alive.
create.sec.port_hint: Reserved for this service, surfaced to the installer as a port variable.
create.sec.python_env_hint: Shared venvs save disk; a private one isolates dependencies.
create.sec.managed_warn: Bespok3d writes the service file. You never ship an init script, so a package cannot smuggle one in.
create.sec.instr_blurb: Only if your plugin has to change a stock Klipper file. You carry a diff and Bespok3d snaps it into place against whatever version is on the printer.
create.sec.no_patch_title: This plugin does not patch Klipper
create.sec.no_patch_body: Most do not. If you need to add a hook to a stock file, author a carried diff and place each hunk by hand. Bespok3d never auto-overwrites a stock file in place.
create.sec.sample_desc: Samples a small region of the toolhead camera feed and exposes the dominant color as a structured event. Pair it with Spoolman to auto-update spool color at load.
create.sec.listing_blurb: What people see in the Store. The card and detail preview show how it reads to an installer.
create.sec.perms_blurb: This is the 'what this will touch' summary your installer confirms. It is built straight from the classes you used, so it can never overstate or understate what the package does.
create.sec.perms_warn: An installer sees exactly this list before installing. Nothing here was typed: it is derived from your files and classes.
create.wb.workbench_sub: Compose a few files into something shareable, or build a full plugin with services and patches. Same engine as a macro, with more of it showing. The drafts below are examples to walk while the authoring engine is wired up.
create.wb.new_plugin_hint: Drop a folder, or start empty (coming soon)
create.wb.buildbar_body: Build a real .b3 and test it on {printer}. The version bumps itself on content change, you never touch a hash.
create.code.explain_title: Show a plain-language note next to each line
create.code.defines_macro: Defines a macro you can call by typing {name}.
create.code.description: A friendly one-liner shown next to the macro.
create.code.gcode_body: Everything indented below runs when the macro is called.
create.code.set_value: Make a value you can reuse below.
create.code.if: Only run the next lines when this is true.
create.code.gcode_g91: Use relative positions (move by an amount)
create.code.gcode_m104: Start heating the nozzle, do not wait
create.code.gcode_m109: Wait for the nozzle to reach temperature
create.code.gcode_m140: Start heating the bed, do not wait
create.code.gcode_m190: Wait for the bed to reach temperature
create.code.gcode_m300: Play a tone on the buzzer
create.code.gcode_respond: Show a message in the console
patchsnap.status_snapped_sub: High-confidence match. The original anchor lines are intact in this update.
patchsnap.status_ambiguous_label: Picks needed: two equally good homes
patchsnap.status_ambiguous_sub: The pre-image matches multiple places. Pick the one you meant.
patchsnap.status_no_match_label: Could not place this one: the context itself was edited
patchsnap.status_no_match_sub: No anchor lines survived in the new version. A hand-merge is needed.
patchsnap.no_partial_matches: No partial matches above noise floor.
patchsnap.help_intro: Bespok3d holds your patch on the right and the updated source on the left. Move the patch until its added lines land in the right place, then apply.
patchsnap.help_1_body_post: handle at the top of the tray to slide all hunks by the same offset.
patchsnap.help_2_title: Nudge one hunk on its own
patchsnap.help_2_body_pre: Each hunk card has its own grip handle and
patchsnap.help_3_title: Follow the cue, click to snap
patchsnap.help_3_body: When a hunk isn't on a strong match, click the sage chip to snap there in one move.
patchsnap.help_4_title: Pick when the match is AMBIGUOUS
patchsnap.help_4_body: The source shows faint candidate labels. Pick the one you meant.
patchsnap.help_5_body_pre: Red hunks couldn't be placed automatically. Click
patchsnap.help_6_body_post: Bump up to see the unified diff and per-offset scores.
patchsnap.help_7_body_post: stays disabled until every hunk is placed.
patchsnap.apply_intro: Review how each hunk landed. Bespok3d writes the result to a fresh branch; nothing on disk is overwritten in place.
patchsnap.auto_snapped_sub: applied as the engine matched them
patchsnap.nudged_into_place_sub: you positioned them; high confidence at release
patchsnap.hand_merged_sub: your edit replaces a chosen source range
patchsnap.revert_pre: The previous branch is kept. Use
patchsnap.slides_all_hunks: slides all {total} hunks by the same offset
patchsnap.applied_toast: Patch applied; branch kept for revert
